newsitem.title: UK: HoF H2 sales up, may close 5-10 stores.
newsitem.headline: HoF H2 sales up, may close 5-10 stores.

text.p: Department store group House of Fraser Plc said like-for-like sales were up 9.2 percent in the first nine weeks of the second half of its current year.

The company said it is in the process of reviewing its stores and "it is currently envisaged that between five and 10 stores, which over the longer term, are unlikely to meet the group's criteria may be sold or closed."

It also reviewing its head office operations with a view to cutting costs. The group said it would make provisions in its full year results for any store closures, stock write-downs and head office cost reductions.
The group said it had seen stronger growth from concessions as a result of a weak performance from "own bought" womenswear, which includes own-label as well as branded merchandise.
During the first half "own bought" ladies wear suffered a 14 percent fall in sales.
The underperformance in "own bought" sales overall was the main reason for a fall in gross margins in the first half to 30.6 percent from 31.2 percent.
Costs also rose in the first half due mainly to rent increases and depreciation.
But menswear sales rose 21 percent and perfumery 12 percent.
Sales from concessions in the stores rose 18 percent, including a 29 percent rise in ladieswear. Concessions accounted for 36 percent of total sales, up from 33 percent in the first half last year.
The proportion of sales via FraserCard rose to 32 percent from 29 percent.
